content: No one is simply wrong: your brother is stressing the life-saving benefit, while your flatmate is stressing bodily autonomy. The real clash is between a public-good, presumed-consent system and the right to control what happens to one’s body. A well-designed opt-out scheme can soften the conflict by making refusal easy and clear, but it still can’t erase the tension.
